issues.failure_explanation: A mixed-base interval with side length b^{-e_j k_j} in coordinate j is itself a base-b elementary interval determined by e_j k_j digits. A digit-wise nested base-b scramble maps such intervals bijectively to intervals of the same mixed-base shape, so it also preserves the (0,e,d)-equidistribution counts. Coarse block scrambling is therefore not necessary merely to preserve this structure.

failure_location.quote: scrambling entire blocks of digits is the natural and necessary way to maintain this structure—a feat not achieved by standard digit-wise scrambling.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the necessity and exclusivity claim, and instead state that both digit-wise and block scrambling preserve the mixed-base equidistribution while inducing different within-block uniformity and gain coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: The stated motivation and claimed structural novelty of coarse scrambling are materially misleading. The formal gain-coefficient results are unaffected.
issues.title: Digit-wise scrambling is falsely said not to preserve the mixed-base structure
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and preserves every formal guarantee, but it withdraws a substantive claimed distinction between the two scrambling methods.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The union of the disjoint sets $L_{\bsl(u,\bsk')}$ over all $\bsk' \le \bsk$ covers exactly the set of all Walsh indices $\bsh$ where $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for all $j \in u$ and $h_j=0$ for $j \notin u$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a singleton u and k=0, the left side is only beta_{u,0}, while the defining inclusion-exclusion gives beta_{u,0}=tilde_beta_{u,u,0}-tilde_beta_{u,emptyset,0}. The subtracted term is the unconditional lower-dimensional mean, so equality with tilde_beta_{u,u,0} fails for a nonconstant function. In the Walsh proof, every relevant L_l has h_j>=1 for j in u, so their union does not include h_j=0 as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the displayed cumulative identity and prove the base-change formula directly as a tensor-product telescoping identity for conditional-expectation differences, keeping the lower-dimensional boundary terms. The appendix union argument must be rewritten accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The identity and its appendix proof are invalid. Consequently the proof of the base-change lemma is unsupported as written, and the subsequent comparison and smooth-rate results lose that link in their proofs.
issues.title: The cumulative ANOVA identity is false
issues.why_classification: The base-change statement is salvageable, but the false identity must be removed and replaced by a contained nontrivial telescoping proof.

issues.failure_explanation: If A_v denotes the raw pair count, then C_{u,v,k}=A_v/n^2 and expansion of the product gives tilde G=n sum_v H_{u,v}C_{u,v,k}, not the displayed sum. Hence the defined G equals sum_v H C_v/prod(b_j-1). The covariance double sum gives variance sum_v H C_v/prod(b_j-1), whereas the theorem supplies G/n, smaller by a factor n. Lemma Cformula likewise equates the normalized C with a raw count.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use one convention consistently: for example, remove the 1/n factor from tilde G and the 1/n^2 factor from C, making both raw pair sums. Then G=raw/[n prod(b_j-1)] and the displayed variance formula and counting computations are consistent.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the variance-gain identity, the explicit counting formula, and every subsequent quantitative gain bound or rate derived from them use incompatible powers of n.
issues.title: Gain and counting normalizations are mutually inconsistent
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced normalization-convention change and preserves the intended gain bounds, variance estimates, and rates without a new mathematical argument.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=0 the point set is empty and both C, with division by n^2, and G, with division by n, are undefined. Thus the universally quantified statements do not hold on their stated domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict n to positive integers, or separately define the empty-point case wherever C or G is used.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary case of the counting lemma and its later restatement for general n is undefined.
issues.title: The counting lemma includes the undefined case n=0
issues.why_classification: Adding the positive-n hypothesis removes the degenerate case without changing any substantive estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $\bsb$ contains exactly one point from $\{\bsx_{rB}, \dots, \bsx_{(r+1)B-1}\}$ where $B := b_1^{k_1} \cdots b_d^{k_d}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Take u={j}, b_j=B, k=0, and n=1, so k'=1. The first B points of an equidistributed sequence fall one per level-1 interval and in distinct level-2 intervals, giving a zero gain kernel sum at n=B. At n=1 the diagonal gain is positive. Thus G_{u,(1)}(B)=0 while G_{u,(1)}(1) is nonzero, contradicting the displayed identity under any positive normalization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete clause (iv), or state and prove a corrected scaling relation from the counting formula; the source supplies no valid replacement identity.
issues.overall_effect: Clause (iv) of the general gain theorem is false as stated.
issues.title: The one-coordinate gain scaling identity is false
issues.why_classification: The false clause is isolated and unused downstream, so removing it leaves the main theorem recognizable, but it necessarily abandons a stated scaling result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $\bsb$ contains exactly one point from $\{\bsx_{rB}, \dots, \bsx_{(r+1)B-1}\}$ where $B := b_1^{k_1} \cdots b_d^{k_d}$.

issues.failure_explanation: With u={j}, b_j=B, k=1, and n=1, the left side is G_{u,(1)}(B), which is zero because the first B equidistributed points occupy distinct level-2 cells while exhausting the B level-1 cells. The right side is G_{u,(0)}(1), which is positive. Hence the identity fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete clause (v), or replace it by a proven corrected relation between gains at different digit levels.
issues.overall_effect: Clause (v) of the general gain theorem is false as stated.
issues.title: The simultaneous digit-level scaling identity is false
issues.why_classification: The remaining gain results do not use this clause, but no source-supported replacement preserves the stated identity.

issues.failure_explanation: The variance-gain theorem contributes a factor 1/n to every term, but the displayed rewrite of the estimator variance omits it. The subsequent bounds for coarse and usual scrambling and the one-dimensional component formulas inherit the same missing 1/b^m factor. This is independent of the separate gain-normalization inconsistency.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the common factor 1/n, respectively 1/b^m, in the variance rewrites and all subsequent variance bounds and component comparisons.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed expressions called variances are too large by a factor n, so the literal bounds do not bound the defined estimators and the rate corollary is not supported by them as written.
issues.title: The comparison variance formulas omit the estimator's 1/n factor
issues.why_classification: The missing factor is common and forced; restoring it leaves the comparisons, constants, and convergence rates unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The variance contains components for every nonempty u, but the assumed full d-dimensional mixed derivative imposes no smoothness on lower-dimensional projections. For example, with d>=2, f(x)=g(x_1) can have the displayed iterated mixed derivative equal to zero by differentiating first in another coordinate, even when g is too rough for n^{-3} variance decay. Thus the cited higher-order scrambling theorem is applied without the needed smoothness of all lower-dimensional faces.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $\partial^df/(\partial x_1 \cdots \partial x_d)$ exists and it is Lipschitz  continuous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to the standard Owen smoothness conditions on every projection, for example existence and Lipschitz continuity of all mixed partial derivatives indexed by u subseteq 1:d, or impose equivalent decay bounds on all sigma_{u,k}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated O(n^{-3}(log n)^{d-1}) guarantee is false for the broad class satisfying only the written hypothesis, and the corresponding abstract rate claim is unsupported.
issues.title: The smoothness hypothesis does not control lower-dimensional ANOVA components
issues.why_classification: A standard but materially stronger hypothesis restores the same rate for smooth integrands without changing the proof architecture; this is a limited loss of the theorem's stated scope.
